kayitlar.title: Conditional requests and rate-limit handling for a GitHub release-polling client
kayitlar.summary: Extends a release-tracking flow with ETag-based conditional requests and with GitHub's documented waiting rules for primary and secondary REST API rate limits.
kayitlar.short_answer: Save each polled response's etag and send it back in if-none-match; an authorized request answered with 304 does not count against the primary limit. Keep query parameters identical between polls and honor x-poll-interval. On 403 or 429, wait for retry-after if present, else until x-ratelimit-reset when remaining is 0, else at least one minute with exponential backoff. Secondary limits cannot be queried.

claims.text: Most REST endpoints return an etag header and many return last-modified, and both can be used for conditional GET requests.
claims.quote: Most endpoints return an etag header, and many endpoints return a last-modified header. You can use the values of these headers to make conditional GET requests.

claims.text: The saved etag value is sent in the if-none-match header on the next request to the same URL.
claims.quote: On your next request to the same URL, send the saved value in the if-none-match header.

claims.text: A 304 response to a correctly authorized conditional request does not count against the primary rate limit.
claims.quote: Making a conditional request does not count against your primary rate limit if a 304 response is returned and the request was made while correctly authorized with an Authorization header.

claims.text: Changing the page size, page number, or filter between polls produces a different etag.
claims.quote: Use the same parameters every time you poll the same data. A different page size, page number, or filter produces a different response with a different etag.

claims.text: When a response includes x-poll-interval, the client should wait at least that many seconds before polling the same endpoint again.
claims.quote: If a response includes an x-poll-interval header, wait at least that many seconds before you poll the same endpoint again.

claims.text: Unauthenticated requests have a primary rate limit of 60 requests per hour.
claims.quote: The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour.

claims.text: Requests made with a user's credentials count toward a personal limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
claims.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

claims.text: Clients should use the x-ratelimit-* headers for pacing but should not depend on an exact remaining count.
claims.quote: Use the x-ratelimit-* response headers to pace and back off your requests, but avoid logic that depends on an exact remaining count.

claims.text: Exceeding the primary limit returns 403 or 429 with x-ratelimit-remaining at 0, and retries should wait until x-ratelimit-reset.
claims.quote: If you exceed your primary rate limit, you will receive a 403 or 429 response, and the x-ratelimit-remaining header will be 0. You should not retry your request until after the time specified by the x-ratelimit-reset header.

claims.text: When a retry-after header is present, the client should not retry before that many seconds have passed.
claims.quote: If the retry-after response header is present, you should not retry your request until after that many seconds has elapsed.

claims.text: Without retry-after or a zero remaining count, the client should wait at least one minute and then back off exponentially for repeated secondary-limit failures.
claims.quote: Otherwise, wait for at least one minute before retrying. If your request continues to fail due to a secondary rate limit, wait for an exponentially increasing amount of time between retries, and throw an error after a specific number of retries.

claims.text: There is no way to check the status of the secondary rate limit.
claims.quote: There is not a way to check the status of your secondary rate limit.

recommendations: Recommendation / inference: keep one stored etag per exact request URL, including per_page and page.

Recommendation / inference: if the releases list returns new releases first, poll only its first page conditionally and fetch further pages after it changes; the sources do not state the list's sort order, so confirm it first.
Recommendation / inference: authenticate polling requests; the 304 exemption needs correct authorization, and the unauthenticated limit is far lower.
Recommendation / inference: send requests one at a time from a single queue, since secondary limits cannot be observed in advance.
Recommendation / inference: apply the waiting rules in the documented order and cap retries.
not_covered: Webhooks, pagination and release semantics (see the companion report).
